text: The partner identity is resolved at the partner gateway and rwb-access keeps no partner table: the gateway authenticates the partner user, resolves the partner user, the partner id and the partner role against rwb-partner, and supplies them to rwb-access as claims of the resolution request. rwb-access answers the internal role model, the scope, the versions and the expiry from role, permission, masking_rule and role_conflict, and reads no S9 table.
why: The Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-6 moves partner, partner_user and partner_instruction to rwb-partner, while legacy RWB-E2-019 resolves the binding inside the access module; without a stated boundary the resolver would either read a foreign table or duplicate the binding, and both break the schema-per-service rule.

text: The resolution is one POST on the rwb-access base, /api/recovery/access/v1/partner-identities/resolve, with the claim set partnerIdentityRef, partnerId, partnerRoleCodes, firmPanelStatus, firmContractEnd, amr, route and tokenExpiry and the answer roles (roleCode, roleClass, letters), scope (type PLACED, partnerId, instructionTypes), matrixVersion, maskingVersion, expiry and decision. Every claim and answer field maps to a DF field of TSD P4 v3 T3.1 or to a claim the gateway asserts, no field is invented as a business value, and the path duplicates no path of rwb-partner.
why: No source names a partner identity operation, a claim set or an answer schema: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A stops at API-P4-021, API Specification v4 has no x-module P4 partner path, and the legacy story publishes a Java interface and no wire shape. The resolver, the gateway and the end-to-end proof cannot build against an open shape.

text: The matrix version and the masking policy version resolve at the moment of resolution and stay for the life of the answer: an answer carries one matrix version and one masking version, a later version does not change an answer in flight, and the next resolution reads the versions then in force. No version is cached beyond the answer and no version is read from another service.
why: The legacy story resolved the session once and revalidated only the binding and the firm; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 carries matrix_version on permission and masking_version on masking_rule with dated versions, and no source states whether a partner session follows a version change mid-session. An unstable answer would let a person see two versions of the matrix in one session.

text: A role conflict refuses the resolution: where the claims name two partner roles, or a partner role held together with a bank role, the answer is a refusal with status 403 and MSG-P4-006 naming both codes, one record carries reason ROLE_CONFLICT, and an incident reaches the security administrator queue. No partial answer is given and no role of the pair is granted.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-019 AC7 and BR2 refuse a partner identity in two partner role groups or in a bank role group and raise an incident, and FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 refuses a conflicting pair with MSG-P4-006; no source states which role survives a conflict, so the only safe default is to refuse rather than to choose.

text: An identity whose claims carry no partner role, an unknown role code or a role of class BANK_USER or NON_HUMAN_ACTOR gets no role at all: the resolution is refused with status 401 and MSG-P4-001 and no scope, no version and no expiry is answered. The unknown or inactive group of the bank identity model is read here as an unknown or inactive partner role claim, and the partner identity reference never becomes a role.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-019 AC4 refuses an identity with no active binding and BR2 binds a partner user to exactly one partner role, and REQ-ACA-012 keeps a partner identity separate from a bank identity; no source says what a claim with no role should receive, and the deny-by-default rule of the architecture leaves no room for a guessed role.

text: rwb-access caches nothing of another service's data and nothing of its own beyond the answer in flight: the claims are used for one answer and discarded, no partner fact is stored, no instruction is cached, and the only retained values are the role, permission, masking_rule and role_conflict rows of rwb_access read on the request. The parameters and reference-data reads are cached no longer than the answer they serve.
why: The legacy story refreshed the binding and the firm status at most every five minutes, which is a cache of another module's data inside the resolver; in the target the firm fact is a claim and the schema-per-service rule leaves nothing to store, so a cache would be an unfounded copy of another owner's state.

text: The access log of a partner resolution is written locally through the local decision-record library and published to rwb.decision-record.v1: a resolution writes one AC-SIGN entry and a refusal writes one AC-DENY entry with its reason, both through the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, and the central ledger and its read stay with rwb-decision. This story writes no decision_log_entry row and no ledger row of its own.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-019 writes an AC-SIGN or an AC-DENY entry for a partner sign-in and a refusal, P7 owns decision_log_entry under the Ownership Map, and DP-03 fixes a local record plus the shared topic as the only shape that both satisfies the audit rule and keeps P4 out of a P7 table.

text: The expiry of a resolution answer is the token expiry the gateway supplies and is never later than it; the gateway issues a sender-constrained access token with a five-minute lifetime, so an answer lives no more than five minutes and a call after it answers 401 with MSG-P4-001. No answer is refreshed silently and no role is served after its expiry.
why: No source states the lifetime of a resolved partner answer: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes a five-minute access token for the partner edge and Architecture v5 slide 35 fixes a short-lived token and a fifteen-minute idle timeout for the staff edge, and the legacy story revalidated on each request instead of bounding an answer. An unbounded answer would outlive the token that justified it.

text: The refusal vocabulary maps to four statuses: 400 for a claim set of the wrong shape with the field named and no message id, 401 for MSG-P4-001 (no partner role, no binding, a bank identity on the partner route, an expired answer) and for MSG-P4-005 (no second factor), 403 for MSG-P4-006 (a role conflict) and MSG-P4-008 (a firm that is not active), and 503 for MSG-P7-003 where the record cannot be written. The four reason strings are BANK_IDENTITY_ON_PARTNER_ROUTE, NO_PARTNER_BINDING, ROLE_CONFLICT and PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE, and no other reason code is declared.
why: The legacy story gives MSG-P4-001 for two different conditions, MSG-P4-005 and MSG-P4-008 without a status, and MSG-P4-006 with an incident; a contract that leaves a refusal without a status cannot be implemented or tested, and inventing a new reason code would invent a business value.

text: The resolution publishes no event and consumes none: the document declares no AsyncAPI message for the capability, names rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 and rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1 as other stories' events, and names rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 only to say that the record of a resolution leaves through the DP-03 library. No inbox, no consumer group and no subscription is declared.
why: Architecture v5 slide 14 calls rwb-access a reference-data owner with no input event and two output events only, TSD P4 v3 T5.3 gives the module no event, and no source states whether a partner resolution announces itself; a capability that declared an event would add a topic contract no other service asked for. The platform observation that suggests a session event is a cache refresh for the reference-data owner, not a partner identity event.

text: The certificate and the trust of the rwb-access hop follow the profile RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes for the partner edge: a certificate valid for 12 months, a rotation inside an overlap window, revocation effective on the thumbprint check immediately and on any cached decision within 30 days at the latest, and a client suspended at its deadline when a rotation fails. The private key is read from the platform key store by reference and never written to a configuration map, an image layer or a log.
why: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes those values for the partner client at the gateway and states that its only upstream is rwb-partner; no source states a profile for the gateway-to-rwb-access hop, and applying one profile to both ends is the only default that does not invent a second security standard for the same edge.

text: The per-client rate limit of the resolution route is the platform limit of the partner gateway, counted per client and per partner identity, with a burst above it and a retry hint in the 429 answer; the limit is not shared with the partner portal route, so a sign-in storm cannot exhaust the instruction traffic and an instruction storm cannot block a sign-in. The numeric value, the burst and the window are set in the gateway configuration baseline and the recorded default is the value the tests use.
why: No source fixes a rate limit for a partner identity call: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes per-client limits for the partner portal route, NFR-003 sizes the partner population at about 50 concurrent users of about 320 named users, and Architecture v5 slide 10 requires a breaker and a bulkhead per downstream. Leaving the call unlimited would let a retry loop at sign-in reach the service that answers authorisation for every screen and service.

text: The network policy is deny by default in both directions and names one namespace, rwb-recovery, one service, rwb-access, and one service port, the port the rwb-access deployment exposes; the only allowed flow is the DMZ egress to that service and port on the resolution path, and no egress to the ACE database, Kafka, the Temporal frontend or another Recovery service is opened. The namespace, the service name and the port are read from the platform deployment rather than fixed as literals in the policy document.
why: Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes one schema, one login and one ACE database and names no Kubernetes service or port, and slide 20 fixes namespace rwb-recovery and the task queue; no source states the NetworkPolicy object, and a policy that wrote a port number as a literal would drift from the deployment.
